html_en:
Claude Code's new Artifacts feature is reshaping how engineering teams communicate — and today's feed makes clear that the tools builders use are quietly becoming as important as the models powering them.

🧩 Claude Code Gets a Living Document Layer

The biggest product news of the day came from Anthropic, which launched Artifacts in Claude Code — a feature that turns an active coding session into a shareable, auto-updating web page. Think incident timelines that refresh themselves as an investigation progresses, PR walkthroughs reviewers can actually follow, or dashboards built from your real infrastructure data. No wiring up data sources, no standing up extra infrastructure.

"New in Claude Code: Artifacts. Interactive pages built from your session, like a PR walkthrough or a living project dashboard, shared with your team at a private link. Available in beta on Team and Enterprise plans." — @claudeai

The feature is currently in beta for Team and Enterprise plans, with Pro and MAX access coming soon. Internal adoption at Anthropic has apparently been swift — Cat Wu noted that it's "changed how we work internally," particularly for communicating architecture changes and new prototypes.

"I've been using Artifacts in Claude Code for everything: visual explanations of tricky code, system diagrams, quick previews of a few animation options, data analyses and dashboards I share with the team. They are a game changer for how I work with Claude." — @bcherny

The privacy architecture is noteworthy: artifacts are private by default, shareable only within an authenticated org, with admin controls, retention policies, and a compliance API. This isn't a consumer toy — it's enterprise collaboration infrastructure built on top of an AI coding session.

⚙️ The Art of Productive Friction in Agent Design

As teams deploy more agentic workflows, a subtler design lesson is emerging: sometimes making the AI ask more questions produces better results than letting it run uninterrupted.

"Early on we were very naive and we thought that the agent could one shot project updates without much input from users. That approach ended up creating a bunch of slop, because users disengaged their brain from the process... By switching to a multi turn interactive mode, the agent prompts you and asks you what to emphasize, what's most important, what context is missing. This simple change elicits much better project updates and ensures that the user has a chance to steer rather than simply being asked to say yes to everything. A very good example of introducing friction for a net benefit." — @thenanyu

It's a principle that cuts against the dominant instinct to minimize latency and maximize autonomy. The best agentic UX, it turns out, may deliberately slow users down at the right moments — keeping human judgment in the loop not through guardrails, but through well-timed questions.

🏗️ The Infrastructure Layer Nobody Talks About

While model releases dominate headlines, Matt Turck went deep on the physical substrate everything runs on. Watch/Listen: The Neocloud Boom: State of AI Compute 2026 | Stephen Balaban. His conversation with Stephen Balaban, cofounder and CTO of Lambda, is an education in why the "GPU compute is a commodity" thesis keeps getting proven wrong.

"Cloud compute is not a commodity service. It is a very complicated, highly vertically integrated type of service that spans everything from land entitlement, construction, HPC design, software, virtualization, cloud services on top. And there's a reason why the biggest companies in the world — whether it's Amazon, Microsoft, Google, Oracle — are all in the cloud computing business. It's because it's a great business." — Stephen Balaban

Balaban's framing of the current moment is striking: we've crossed a threshold where the economics of software production have been permanently altered.

"It's pretty clear that we have an amazing system that can take in money and output software... we continue to see no end to the scaling laws."

On whether we're overbuilding: Balaban is unequivocal that we're not — demand for compute remains "insatiable," and the real bottlenecks are land, power, and construction timelines, not capital or willingness to spend.

⚖️ Open Weights, Regulation, and the Applied AI Layer

Two policy-adjacent threads ran through the feed today. First, the news that frontier open-weights models are approaching closed-model capability levels prompted Aaron Levie to articulate what this means for the broader ecosystem:

"The fact that open weights models are being discussed credibly at this level of capability should be a huge update for many. The implications of open models getting to frontier performance ensures that you can always have sovereign AI, have the ability to post train for your specific workflows, cost optimize for various workloads, and actually afford to do much more with AI — which opens up meaningfully different applications. Huge win for the applied AI layer." — @levie

On the regulatory front, Levie also weighed in on what government frameworks for model releases might look like — noting that while review processes could slow the rapid iteration pace the industry has grown accustomed to, they might also push labs to bundle improvements into bigger, less frequent jumps. Meanwhile, Garry Tan was characteristically direct about a proposed bill from Bernie Sanders that would seize 50% equity in AI startups crossing $200M in revenue:

"Bernie Sanders introduced a bill to seize 50% of any AI startup that crosses $200M in revenue. The same anti-prosperity bloc spent the year trying to ban startup acquisitions, blocking the only exit 85% of founders ever get. This is a war on building startups in America." — @garrytan

The legislative proposal is unlikely to advance, but the political signal it sends — that AI's commercial success is becoming a target — is worth watching as the industry scales.
html_zh:
Claude Code 今天推出了 Artifacts 功能，将 AI 编程助手从单纯的代码生成工具升级为团队协作平台——与此同时，关于 AI 算力基础设施的讨论也在持续升温，整个行业正在重新思考"构建"究竟意味着什么。

🧩 Claude Code 的 Artifacts：从代码到协作页面

今天最重磅的产品新闻来自 Anthropic。Claude Code 正式推出 Artifacts 功能，让 AI 编程会话的产出不再只是代码——而是可以实时更新、团队共享的可视化页面。PR 演练、系统架构图、事故复盘报告、数据仪表盘，都可以由 Claude Code 自动生成并发布到一个私有链接，随着会话推进自动刷新。

"新的 Claude Code 功能：Artifacts。从你的会话中生成的交互式页面——比如 PR 演练或实时项目仪表盘——通过私有链接与团队共享。"
— @claudeai

Anthropic 工程师 @bcherny 第一时间分享了内部体验：

"我已经把 Artifacts 用在了所有地方：复杂代码的可视化解释、系统架构图、几种动画方案的快速预览、与团队分享的数据分析和仪表盘。这彻底改变了我与 Claude 的协作方式。"

@_catwu 补充说，这个功能已经改变了 Anthropic 内部的工作方式，尤其适合传达架构变更和新原型。目前 Artifacts 以 beta 版本向 Claude Team 和 Enterprise 计划开放，Pro 和 MAX 计划即将跟进。

⚙️ 智能摩擦：Agent 设计的微妙之道

产品功能之外，一个更深层的设计哲学问题正在引发讨论：AI Agent 应该尽量减少用户干预，还是适时引入"摩擦"？

@thenanyu 分享了一段颇具启发性的实践反思：

"早期我们非常天真，以为 Agent 可以在几乎没有用户输入的情况下一次性完成项目更新。结果产出了大量'垃圾'，因为用户的大脑完全脱离了写作过程。

改为多轮交互模式后，Agent 会主动追问你想强调什么、什么最重要、缺失了哪些背景。这个简单的改变大幅提升了项目更新的质量，确保用户有机会主导方向，而不仅仅是被动地说'是'。

这是一个很好的例子——引入摩擦，反而带来净收益。"

这与 Claude Code Artifacts 的设计理念形成了有趣的呼应：真正有价值的 AI 协作，不是让人类消失在流程之外，而是让人类更有效地参与其中。

🏗️ 算力基础设施：永远在"供不应求"

Watch/Listen: The Neocloud Boom: State of AI Compute 2026 | The MAD Podcast with Matt Turck

Matt Turck 与 Lambda 联合创始人兼 CTO Stephen Balaban 的对话，是今天关于 AI 算力基础设施最值得深读的一手资料。核心论点鲜明：GPU 算力从来就不是、也不会成为商品。

"现在已经非常清楚：我们拥有一个神奇的系统，可以把钱投进去，然后输出软件。那些唱衰者说'这些 GPU 五年后就会被淘汰'，他们完全错了，而且一直都错了。我们整体上仍然处于供给不足的状态，对大语言模型的需求似乎看不到尽头。"
— Stephen Balaban

Balaban 特别指出，外界对 GPU 租赁价格"下跌"的判断存在方法论错误——彭博 H100 价格指数混淆了长期合同与短期按需价格，而实际上两者都在上涨。他的判断是：算力市场的竞争格局将类似于传统云计算，形成多强并立的寡头格局，而非赢者通吃。

⚖️ 监管风暴与开源红利

政策层面的紧张态势也在今天集中爆发。Garry Tan 对参议员 Bernie Sanders 提出的法案发出强烈批评——该法案拟对营收超过 2 亿美元的 AI 初创公司没收 50% 股权：

"这是一场针对美国创业公司的战争。"

与此同时，Aaron Levie 对 AI 监管框架的到来保持了相对冷静的态度，认为政府介入"几乎是必然"，但对结果抱有谨慎乐观：

"一个积极的可能未来是：我们仍然能看到巨大的模型进步，只是进步方式变成了更大幅度的跳跃——因为每次审查的成本和延迟会促使实验室把重大改进集中打包推出。"

另一方面，Levie 对开源模型的崛起表示欢迎：

"开源权重模型正在被认真讨论，且具备前沿级别的能力——这对很多人来说应该是一个重大的认知更新。开源模型的含义是：你永远可以拥有主权 AI，可以针对特定工作流进行后训练，可以为不同负载优化成本，真正让你'用得起'AI。这对应用层来说是巨大的胜利。"

💡 今日一语

@steipete 用一句话概括了当下 AI 产品体验的分野，简洁而精准：

"现在所有东西要么是快 API，要么是慢 API。"

Claude Code Artifacts 的"实时刷新"与 Fable 等尚未解锁的能力之间的张力，或许正是这句话最好的注脚。Dan Shipper 半开玩笑地说，等 Fable 解锁之前，"不如先去度假"——而这背后，是整个行业对下一个生产力跃迁的真实期待。
